clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 to buy an apple orchard, within the year: June became homesick and wrote to her sister daily, then kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter spent long hours in the trees away from June, and the two had rows over money for new trees; Glen got into fights at his new school; Walter cut off his brother Harlan over a quarrel about their father's land money. By September 1953, June had joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, and her anxiety dropped. The shifts cluster around the move and its first year in the valley.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily most nights, and he and Glen blamed each other for the loss. Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Glen began at the cannery in February 1969. Glen's son Carl developed worse asthma that winter. You began wetting the bed again in April 1969. By October 1969, Walter had stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, his functioning up. The shifts run from the loss through the auction and the family's move to Ridgeport.

clusters.name: Glen's cannery closing, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat in the truck in the yard for hours most of that year, his functioning down; he and Marian had loud fights over money at night; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night. You stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer. You kept to your room and said little to your mother. Walter began drinking again after six years off it. By June 1976, you were eating again and made the track team, your functioning up.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: you and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, and took his mother's side; your son Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma took over Lily's care; you developed eczema on both hands; you and Hollis had rows most nights. You drove over twice a week to take your mother's side. In June 1991, Wilma took a flat in town, and by August your eczema had cleared. The shifts run from Wilma's arrival through her move out.

declined.reason: 1994: An acute episode. All shifts fall within four days around the wildfire evacuation, from August 12 to August 16, 1994. You were frightened and kept the children in sight; Lily was sick to her stomach in the gym; Owen would not sleep without a light on; you snapped at Hollis over whether to drive out. By August 16 you were allowed home and within a week you were calm again and the children were back at school. This is a brief flare around a real threat, not a period.
